courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: What is state? When I say state,
I basically mean data,
I mean data that we use in our application in different ways and also different kinds of data.
I like to think of state as one of three things.
First, there is something which I like to call user interface state, UI state,
then there also is temporary or local state and persistent state.
Now these are really just terms I came up with,
it's not a hard definition or anything like that but these are the three categories of data or state
we're working with in our application.
Now what do I mean with each category?
User Interface state means answers to questions like, are we loading something.
So if in a component, we're having an isLoading property and we're setting this property to true
when we start fetching data from a server and we set it to false once we're done and we're using that
data to then show a spinner, then we're effectively using the user interface state because the state of this
component and of what we render on the user interface changed, we showed a spinner whilst we're loading
data. Now this is not a state that affects our entire application, it affects the page we're on because
there we want to show a spinner and therefore this is what I like to call UI state because it influences
the user interface and it's managed instead of the component that is responsible for rendering
that part of the user interface. Now temporary or local state is a bit more than that,
this could be for example a list of loaded events. Now such a list could be used in different places
of our application. We could have a component, a page where we render that list
but when we then added one of the items, we basically use data from that same list you could say and
therefore, this typically is data which we manage inside of services in an Angular application because
services in Angular are our cross-component communication vehicles if you want to call them like
this and they're also perfect for letting a component know that our state changed. Now last but not least,
we have that concept or that thing which I like to call persistent state.
Now what's that? Well the list of loaded events for example would be data we use in the app and we load
these events whenever we added a new one or when our application starts. Now
the persistent state is basically our data, our state that must not get lost by the user or closing
the application or even by uninstalling the application.
If you're using Facebook, you don't want to lose all your friends just because you uninstalled the Facebook
app and therefore this could also be the list of all the events but not just of the events we loaded
in our application, even if we happened to load all
but here, I really mean the data that we definitely need for our application and that glues together
our application and therefore, this is typically not managed inside of the app or in memory or not
even on onDeviceStorage where it could get lost if the user erases his device but on a back-end, on
a server in a database there.
So this is decoupled from our app but of course still in our app, we write code to fetch our data from
there and to save it on a server.
Now for all that data management with a back-end, with a server, with a database, I'll have a separate
module so we'll not focus on that type of state in this module. We'll focus on the UI state and the temporary
and local state in this module,
so therefore let's dive in and let's have a look at our application and use all that user input we're fetching
already.
